comparison: Perfect agreement on dynamin requirement (C58-C60). Both evaluations find the evidence convincing using multiple complementary approaches (siRNA, dominant-negative, pharmacological inhibitors). Peer reviewers explicitly accept dynamin as essential machinery.

Perfect agreement on endosomal marker characterization (C37-C39). Both accept the temporal progression from early to late endosomal markers. OpenEval notes heterogeneous marker distribution makes definitive classification difficult; peer reviewers acknowledge molecular characterization 'has been advanced, although not fully resolved.'

Strong agreement on functional significance for cell survival and anoikis protection (C11, C74, C76-C80, C82-C83, C86-C87). Both evaluations emphasize multiple complementary assays and genetic loss-of-function experiments. Peer reviewers explicitly state this work contributes to understanding cell survival mechanisms against anoikis.

Strong agreement on septin requirement (C51-C57, C102). Both evaluations accept the evidence from localization studies, pharmacological inhibition, genetic depletion, and domain deletion experiments. Peer reviewers explicitly identify septin as essential machinery with no concerns raised.

Strong agreement on macropinocytosis-like mechanism (C7, C40-C49, C101). Both evaluations praise multi-modal evidence including TEM, super-resolution imaging, and live imaging demonstrating plasma membrane invagination. Peer reviewers explicitly describe this as 'macropinocytosis-like process' using 'cutting edge cell biology techniques.'

Strong agreement on PI3K requirement and PI(3)P role in fusion (C61-C73, C103). Both evaluations emphasize comprehensive evidence from pharmacological inhibition, siRNA, CRISPR/Cas9, and lipid probe localization. Peer reviewers particularly praise the knockdown/knockout experiments added in revision, noting PI3P requirement for vesicle fusion.

Agreement on speculative nature of clinical relevance claims (C104-C105). Both evaluations recognize these as hypotheses requiring future investigation. OpenEval explicitly labels as 'UNCERTAIN' and notes no direct evidence for CTCs forming GUVacs in vivo. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate CTC speculation but accept speculative discussion as appropriate.

Strong agreement on specificity controls (C23-C28, plus C8, C35-C36, C48 in peer evaluation). Both evaluations accept negative controls demonstrating specificity to actin depolymerization. Peer reviewers acknowledge authors addressed concerns about drug reliance by adding canonical cell biology approaches in revision.

Strong agreement on core finding of actin depolymerization-induced GUVac formation (C4-C6, C21-C22, C29, C32-C34, plus additional claims in peer evaluation including C7, C19-C20, C30-C31, C100). Both evaluations emphasize converging evidence from multiple experimental approaches. Peer reviewers explicitly state evidence is 'convincing' with 'comprehensive analysis' and 'clean data.'

Agreement on protection from extrinsic apoptosis (C81, C93). Both evaluations accept the FasL experiments. OpenEval notes mechanism is not explored; peer reviewers accept the finding as part of overall cell survival data without distinguishing between death stimuli. C94 speculation addressed separately.

Strong agreement on reversibility (C84, with C85 also in peer evaluation). Both evaluations accept time-lapse imaging evidence. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'this process is reversible' as a strength. OpenEval notes molecular mechanisms of GUVac breakdown are not explored.

Agreement on matrix attachment requirement (C35-C36). OpenEval provides dedicated evaluation noting critical contextual requirement with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers include these claims in broader specificity controls evaluation, accepting the finding without specific concerns.

Agreement on tissue-specific competence (C30-C31). OpenEval notes systematic testing across cell lines but limited sample of non-secretory types and unexplored mechanistic basis. Peer reviewers include these claims in overall positive evaluation of the core finding without raising specific concerns about tissue specificity.

Agreement on baseline quantification (C19-C20). OpenEval provides dedicated evaluation noting this establishes low frequency in control conditions. Peer reviewers include these claims in comprehensive evaluation of the core finding, accepting the baseline data as part of overall characterization.

Agreement on distinction from entosis (C100). OpenEval provides dedicated evaluation noting morphological distinction is important for establishing GUVacs as distinct phenomenon. Peer reviewers include this claim in overall positive evaluation, implicitly accepting the distinction as part of the 'interesting and potentially important observation.'
